newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danes say Scandinavian air pact good through 2020.
newsitem.headline: Danes say Scandinavian air pact good through 2020.

text.p: Denmark, Norway and Sweden intend to retain a joint policy on aviation and maintain their partnership in Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) until at least the year 2020 although further SAS privatisation could take place earlier, a Danish government paper said on Tuesday.
"The Scandinavian transport ministers agree to extend Scandinavian air transport co-operation and SAS collaboration until 2020," said a draft bill put before the cabinet.
"It is also agreed that new policy on state ownership of the national (SAS) companies can develop, whereas ownership is now split equally between state and private investment," it added.
The SAS group is comprised of three national units; SAS Danmark A/S and SAS Norge ASA, each holding two-sevenths of the group equity, and SAS Sverige AB, with a three-sevenths stake.
Each of the three entities is owned 50 percent by its national government and 50 percent by private investors.
"In the event of proposals for change there will be close contact between the ministers, who will discuss the issue before changes are approved," the Danish bill said.
It also pledged to pursue "open skies" treaties with European Union and European Economic Area member states.
